physical_conclusions: 1. Detector-name precision ranking is completely debunked: Array B (Gammasphere-class legacy array with lower Q=0.20 but N=100k and sigma_a/a=0.5%) achieves Fisher information I_F = 56.21 and decisive Bayes factor B = 999999.0, whereas Array A (AGATA-class tracking array with higher Q=0.28 but low stats N=4k and sigma_a/a=1.5%) achieves only I_F = 5.89 and weak Bayes factor B = 685.4.
2. Precision is a property of the full likelihood contract L(delta | D, C) including statistics N, background B, calibration sigma_a, and sensitivity sigma_Q, NOT the nominal array generation.

3. Shared instrumental calibrations induce strictly positive covariance Cov(P1, P2) = 0.000227 (correlation rho = 0.397) across transitions in the same band network; omitting this covariance falsely inflates multi-transition mode discrimination significance.

4. Near marginal polarization boundaries, the likelihood profile L(delta) is distinctly bimodal (peaks at delta = -1.81 and 0.08); forcing a symmetric Gaussian error delta = delta_bar +/- sigma_delta is mathematically unjustified and creates spurious mode exclusion.
